### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/driver-turso`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **63** documentable anchor(s).

**12** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/environment-routing.mdx`  _(via createStandaloneStack (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via os migrate organization-ownership (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/organization-ownership.ts))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/drivers.mdx`  _(via TursoDriver (symbol, a top-level class), createStandaloneStack (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/indexing.mdx`  _(via recreate_index (literal, a string literal in applyRemoteIndexDriftOp))_
- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via create_index (literal, a string literal in applyRemoteIndexDriftOp), drop_index (literal, a string literal in applyRemoteIndexDriftOp), recreate_index (literal, a string literal in applyRemoteIndexDriftOp), replace_unique_index (literal, a string literal in applyRemoteIndexDriftOp), sys_migration (literal, a string literal in runApply), os migrate organization-ownership (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/organization-ownership.ts))_

- `content/docs/deployment/single-project-mode.mdx`  _(via createStandaloneStack (symbol, a top-level function))_

- `content/docs/plugins/packages.mdx`  _(via TursoDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via sys_migration (literal, a string literal in runApply))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-4.mdx`  _(via sys_migration (literal, a string literal in runApply))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `defaultValue (literal, 32 pages)`
- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **46** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1eac7ad751e833115544be405993efced6a726d3` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `53854f3f87b584651bbbad95c4c944930a2969d8` — the merge of head `26b6acefac48d6afbc4706c33a7835b285b1bed1` into base `1eac7ad751e833115544be405993efced6a726d3`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 53854f3f87b584651bbbad95c4c944930a2969d8 && git checkout 53854f3f87b584651bbbad95c4c944930a2969d8
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 1eac7ad751e833115544be405993efced6a726d3 26b6acefac48d6afbc4706c33a7835b285b1bed1 && git checkout -B drift-repro 1eac7ad751e833115544be405993efced6a726d3 && git merge --no-ff 26b6acefac48d6afbc4706c33a7835b285b1bed1

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1eac7ad751e833115544be405993efced6a726d3
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 1eac7ad751e833115544be405993efced6a726d3` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review: CHANGES REQUESTED (head `39b9abdda3`)

The PM for #23816 recorded this review on 2026-10-16 from the maintainer's local session. It is read-only and reviewed against merge-base `43567a8f`.

**The ceremony fix itself passes.**
- No spec key moved, and the remote face's answers have the file face's shapes.
- `applyMigrationEntries` executes only the declared kinds.
- Each `drop_column` is one libSQL write batch, which rolls back as a whole.
- Skipped entries count as `failed` in `organization-ownership-column-drops.ts`.
- Identifiers are quoted and catalog reads are parameterized.
- `skip-schema-sync` is reached only from the ceremony's two call sites, and only when the resolved primary is a Turso remote.

### Blocking 1: the `OS_ARTIFACT_URL` boot migration gate now refuses healthy remote deployments
- **Cause:** the remote face's `buildCreateTableSQL` / `ADD COLUMN` never emit `NOT NULL`. driver-turso has zero `notNull` references at this head; driver-sql has thirteen files. A field declared `storage: { notNull: true }` is created nullable on a remote database.
- **What the differ reports:** `tighten_not_null`, category `destructive` (`schema-drift.ts`). This was measured on the shared differ: TEXT nullable column + `storage.notNull` → `[{op:'tighten_not_null',category:'destructive'}]`; without `storage` → `[]`.
- **Result:** with this PR, `os serve` / `os start` with `OS_ARTIFACT_URL` and a `libsql://` primary (a documented self-hosting combination) refuses to boot on a freshly synced database.
  - Its remedy, `os migrate apply --allow-destructive`, refuses on the remote transport too.
  - HotCRM declares `storage.notNull` widely (e.g. `src/sales/objects/lead.object.ts`).
  - Before this PR the gate warned that it could not check, and booted.

**Maintainer's ruling** (2026-10-16, verbatim: the option 「恢复警告并补测试」): on a Turso remote primary, restore the gate's earlier answer, "cannot judge, warn and boot". Do not auto-apply and do not refuse. Decide it from the declared capability, not by comparing the `transportMode` string. The gate judges remote databases again only after the two follow-ups below land. Say this plainly in the changeset (today it reads "widening" only).

### Blocking 2: the embedded-replica control was lost with the deleted refusal test
The removed `turso-remote-drift-detection-refusal.test.ts` also pinned that the **embedded-replica** face reports drift on a drifted database. No remaining test covers that, and the PR names no replacement (AGENTS.md: a deleted test names its same-layer or closer duplicate). Add one replica case.

### Required in this PR (the maintainer accepted these with the ruling)
3. **Pure unit tests** so CI guards the CLI half without `OS_TEST_SQLD_BIN`:
   - the ceremony's two `deferredDdlUnsupported: 'skip-schema-sync'` opt-ins;
   - `transportRefusesDeferredDdl`;
   - the primary exemption (`exemptPrimary`).
   Today any of the three can break with CI still green.
4. The sqld e2e stays opt-in. No new CI dependency (open question 2 → B).

### Follow-ups, not in this PR
- **Open question 1** is answered by the ruling above (B, until the follow-ups land).
- **Two cards are filed separately:**
  - the remote face honours `storage.notNull` on create / add column;
  - a remedy path for destructive drift on a remote database (`os migrate apply` on the remote face).
- **Non-blocking notes:**
  - `turso-driver.ts` cites a non-existent `turso-local-remote-drift-parity.test.ts`; the real file is `turso-remote-drift-detection.test.ts`.
  - `remoteCatalogRead` folds a non-array result into `[]`, a latent "no drift". Prefer a throw.
  - The applied read-back for `create_index` / `replace_unique_index` checks the name only, and the doc overstates it.
  - The remote no-argument probe makes about 4 sequential round trips per table, so roughly 440 on a ~110-table tenant. Consider `batch(…,'read')`; cloud's first-request upgrade pays this.

After the changes, push and re-run the gates. The PM re-reviews the increment and clears `needs:contract-review` on a PASS.

Pointer to the review above: the two follow-ups are filed as #23847 (the remote face honours `storage.notNull` on create / add column) and #23848 (`os migrate apply` on a Turso remote database). Until both land, the `OS_ARTIFACT_URL` gate stays warn-and-boot on a remote primary. In the changeset, refer to them as follow-ups, not as closed by this PR.

## Contract review
Served-tier: TIER_DEFAULT
Head: `26b6acefac48d6afbc4706c33a7835b285b1bed1` (round 1 reviewed `39b9abdda3`, CHANGES REQUESTED in comment 6211456559)
Implemented-by: os-dev `session_01Lr3rg6qTp9r38exA5DHEEH` · Reviewed-by: contract-review subagent of the #23816 PM session (separate read-only session)
Local-runs:
- round 1: a probe of the shared differ over a prebuilt driver-sql dist (`storage.notNull` over a nullable column → `tighten_not_null`, destructive);
- round 2: none.

① **Contract surface.** No `packages/spec` change; only widenings:
- the Turso remote face's `detectManagedDrift` / `applyMigrationEntries` now answer instead of 501, with the file face's return shapes and skip-and-warn semantics;
- `TursoDriver.driftReportCaveat`, `RemoteTransport.batch` / `createIndexSql`, and `StandaloneStackConfig.skipSchemaSync` are new.

The new CLI symbols (`DeferSchemaDdlPlugin`, `transportRefusesDeferredDdl`, `SqlDriverLike.driftReportCaveat`) cannot be reached from the cli exports map. Only `os migrate organization-ownership` (plan and apply) opts into skip-schema-sync.

② **Semver.** Minor for driver-turso, cli and runtime, matching the changeset. On a Turso remote primary the `OS_ARTIFACT_URL` gate keeps warn-and-boot through the declared caveat: no detect, no apply, no refusal. Local, replica and the other SQL drivers are unchanged.

③ **Round-1 flags resolved:**
- the gate is restored (`artifact-boot-migration.ts:134-138`, with a null-caveat control);
- the embedded-replica control is back as the same-layer replacement for the deleted refusal suite's replica case;
- two unit suites pin the CLI posture in CI, and the ablations are consistent.

The PR body is updated to round 2. Follow-ups #23847 and #23848 stay OPEN.

**Non-blocking, recorded for later:**
- `create_index` read-back does not compare NULL-safe / partial shape;
- the "3 round trips" holds up to 100 tables;
- `remoteCatalogSnapshot` is instance state that two concurrent detects could leave stale (no reader today).

PASS
